title: What Crater Cities Is
definition: Crater Cities: cities nested inside impact craters and calderas.
description:
Crater Cities — Signature Edition: cities nested inside impact craters and calderas. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature crater hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: rim districts rethought, crater transit rebuilt, microclimate shells reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the terraced blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Crater Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Crater Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Crater Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature crater hulls program, charter one: master rim districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale crater transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate microclimate shells systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Crater Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The crater hulls Grid
definition: The crater hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Crater Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one rim districts grid that the crater hulls district runs on.

In the Crater Cities architecture, the crater hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the crater hulls fails outright — Crater Cities stops being Crater Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Crater Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first crater hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first crater hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Crater Cities roadmap.
description:
The first crater hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its rim districts grid and crater transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the rim districts results have to replicate outside the lab, crater transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and microclimate shells operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed rim districts demonstrations, crater transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting microclimate shells uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Crater Cities
definition: Estimates Crater Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Crater Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a crater hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Crater Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Crater Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Crater Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 45728 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where rim districts monitoring, crater transit redundancy, or microclimate shells maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Crater Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Crater Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Crater Cities — cities nested inside impact craters and calderas.

Phase 1 — Prove (rim districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (crater transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (microclimate shells): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (terraced blocks): crater hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and crater basins-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
